questions.explain: Four sources: direct user injection, indirect injection via retrieved RAG documents, tool-output injection from web/API results, and multi-turn erosion that gradually steers past constraints — each needs its own defense.
options: Direct user injection, indirect injection via retrieved documents, tool-output injection, and multi-turn erosion
Prompt injection is not a real threat
questions.q: What are the four prompt-injection threat vectors?

questions.explain: The cheapest defenses don't depend on model smarts: delimit untrusted content in explicit tags, give agents least-privilege allowlisted parameterized tools, and let RLS be the final backstop so injection escalates within a tenant, never across tenants.
options: Delimit untrusted content, least-privilege tools, and RLS as the cross-tenant backstop
Rely on the model being smart

questions.explain: Screen inputs (quarantine suspicious documents with is_suspicious=1, excluded from retrieval pending review), validate outputs against security rules, and plant canary tokens in the system prompt — a canary in a response means injection succeeded.
options: Input screening with suspicious-document quarantine, output validation, and canary tokens that trigger alerts
questions.q: How do detection and filtering (Layer 2) work?

questions.explain: Assume injection succeeds: per-session tool-call budgets, rate limits, and approval gates bound the blast radius; a kill switch invalidates the session and cancels runs; canary trips feed a Service Broker incident pipeline that pages on-call.
options: Blast-radius caps, session kill switch, and an incident pipeline — with every decision in the audit trail
questions.q: What is the containment strategy when injection succeeds?

questions.explain: Red-team quarterly testing the database layer too: an injection battery (direct, indirect, tool-output, multi-turn), exfiltration probes verifying the RLS backstop, and cost attacks — every fixed vulnerability becomes a permanent CI regression test.
options: Red-team quarterly across all layers including the database, and add every fixed vulnerability to CI as a regression test
Only test the model, not the database

title: Securing AI Apps Against Prompt Injection
